rules: Pool

Each Hero owns 20 designs with two physical copies of each: 40 cards. Choose any 24. You may take 0, 1 or 2 of each design. Each Hero’s pool includes their own physical copies of the ten shared Basic designs. No Basic/Hero quota; no shared Basic draw pile.
Setup

Choose one of three Fury cards and reveal that choice beside your Hero. It is outside the 24-card deck. Shuffle the 24 and draw 7. Start at 20 Health, 0 Coins, spaces 3 and 5. Randomly give one player Edge; it changes sides after every round.
Choose attacks

Commit two attack-capable cards in order if able. If you have only one, use the first slot; if none, leave both empty. Empty slots pass. An out-of-range Attack is still an eligible Attack. All other cards remain in hand. A committed dual-use card is locked as an Attack and cannot also react.
Reveal and react

Reveal the first pair together. Higher Speed activates first; Edge breaks ties. Resolve its Activate text, then the defender reacts first. Alternate one Reaction, one Loot, or pass. Played Reactions and Loot resolve immediately. Two consecutive passes resolve the active Attack using current positions. A card play resets passes; one pass does not prevent reacting later. Give the other Attack its own exchange, then reveal pair 2. If a pair has one Attack, resolve just that Attack; if none, skip the pair.
Dual-use cards

Play exactly one half, then discard the card after its effect finishes. Reaction text marked Attacking is only usable during your own active Attack; Defending only during your rival’s active Attack; Either in either exchange. Neither Reaction Speed nor a second Attack is created by a Reaction half. You may play a legal Reaction for little or no benefit, such as Move 0, but cannot ignore its printed timing or Range requirement just to empty your hand.
Movement

All Move values mean up to that many spaces, chosen when the effect resolves. You can stay, move either direction, or cross your rival, but never finish on their space. Push moves the rival away; pull moves them toward you without crossing or sharing your space. Choose the distance when resolving. Range is the difference between the occupied space numbers.
Range and bonuses

Use the printed Attack range, then modifiers. Alf’s passive tests printed minimum Range, even when Trick Shot changes effective minimum Range. Maximum-range bonuses never change minimum Range. Damage bonuses and ignored Block add together and last only for the current Attack. Every Attack here hits once. No extra reactions occur between the hit and its on-hit push/pull.
Hit and Block

An Attack hits only if it deals at least 1 Health damage to its rival. On-hit movement does not occur after a miss or full Block. Block is spent preventing damage, is capped at 6 and clears for both players after each active Attack. Ignore N Block leaves up to N existing Block unused for this hit; it does not destroy Block. All Block still clears when the Attack ends.
Wall slam

A chosen push that would go beyond space 1 or 7 stops at the edge and deals 1 extra damage ignoring Block (Smasherton: 2, upgraded: 3). Landing exactly on the edge deals none. One push effect causes at most one slam, regardless of unused distance. Combine a single Attack’s printed push and bonus push into one push effect. A Reaction push is a separate effect and can slam immediately; pulls never slam.
Coins and Loot

A Basic Attack earns 1 Coin when it finishes, including a miss; cap 8 Coins. Basic Reactions, Hero cards and Fury earn none. After the round, each player may buy one blind Loot for 2 Coins if holding fewer than two. Loot stays outside the seven-card hand/refill. Use the existing Loot effects as the control for the first test, with two physical copies of each of the 12 designs: 24 shared Loot cards. No new Loot designs in this pass.
Refill

After all committed Attacks finish, discard spent cards and keep unused hand cards. Draw up to 4, stopping at a hand of 7. No voluntary discard. If you still have 5 cards, draw 2; if you have 2, draw 4 and begin with 6. A printed draw effect may exceed the limit. No automatic draws during combat. When a draw pile runs out, shuffle its spent discard to continue; never include held or committed cards.
Fury at 10

The first time you have 10 or less Health and are still alive, put the chosen Fury into your hand. This is an extra draw and may take you over 7. It can be committed at the next planning step, never inserted into the current round’s locked Attacks. Once played, it goes to your normal discard and can return on a later reshuffle. Its threshold does not trigger twice.
Upgrade at 5

The first time you have 5 or less Health and are still alive, permanently upgrade the Hero passive. Healing never removes either unlock. If a single damage event crosses both thresholds, unlock both. Reaching 0 ends the game immediately; there is no Fury rescue. For future Heroes, Health payments count toward thresholds and must be costed with that interaction in mind.
End and anti-stall

Health 0 means immediate defeat. Retain the existing safety valve for the first comparison: at round-10 cleanup both lose 2 Health ignoring Block, increasing by 1 each subsequent round up to 18; simultaneous defeat is a draw. This is a testing backstop, not a target fight length.

builds.name: Relentless Pursuit
builds.plan: Use printed movement to start the chase, and keep one movement Reaction to answer the escape. Buy Loot with Quick Jab, Lunge or Advance when a Hero hit is not worth spending.
builds.sequence: Bull Rush moves 2 before reactions. If Alf retreats, Hammer Dash moves 2 and makes that Attack hit for 5. Shoulder Check can add one more step, but spending both chase cards leaves less defence and a smaller refill.
builds.weakness: Only two Brace/Bear Hug copies combined. Repeatedly spending three Reactions in one round shrinks the next hand.
builds.why: The first Smasherton deck to try: multiple ways into melee, mixed damage speeds and real Basic income.

builds.name: Wall Demolition
builds.plan: Herd the rival toward an end space; save your damage bonus until a push can actually exceed the edge. A push that lands exactly on space 7 is setup, not a wall slam.
builds.sequence: At positions 5 and 6, Uppercut plus Wrecking Ball hits for 6, then can push 3. A full push exceeds space 7 and adds one 2-damage wall slam: 8 Health lost with no Block. After the 5-Health upgrade, 9.
builds.weakness: Can push Alf out of the second committed Attack’s range. Lower income than the pursuit list; wall Reactions can be dead away from contact.
builds.why: Tests whether walls create satisfying tactical payoffs or excessive instant damage.

builds.name: Paid to Smash
builds.plan: Resolve Basic Attacks to buy one blind Loot whenever affordable. Save the Hero amplifiers and a movement card for a hit that matters.
builds.sequence: A Basic Heavy Blow plus Hammer Dash is 6 damage after a 2-space chase and still earns a Coin. The same cards can fuel The Last Word later, but Fury never earns a Coin.
builds.weakness: Only Guarded Strike supplies Block. Loot is random: the build must function before the desired item appears.
builds.why: A deliberate economy-heavy stress test: can Coins compete with a denser Hero package without becoming the mandatory best route?

builds.name: Keep Them Chasing
builds.plan: Use Attack movement for the first reposition and hold a Reaction for the pursuit. Keep useful Basics to pay for surprise Loot.
builds.sequence: Vaulting Shot moves 2 on activation. If Smasherton chases into Range 1, Grapple can reopen distance during Alf’s own Attack; Backflip Shot’s Reaction cannot, because it is defending-only.
builds.weakness: Damage is lower than the sniper build. Spending every escape to avoid chip damage can empty the hand before an important shot.
builds.why: The first Alf deck to try: broad access to movement, with meaningful decisions about when to spend it.

builds.name: One Perfect Shot
builds.plan: Make one ranged hit worth the commitment. Keep Trick Shot for a close chase or Grapple to reopen the dead zone; these solve different problems.
builds.sequence: Power Shot plus Perfect Aim hits for 7 and ignores 2 Block. If Smasherton reaches Range 1, Trick Shot can bring minimum Range down to 1; its printed minimum of 3 still qualifies it for Long Shot.
builds.weakness: Less built-in movement and fewer close Attacks. The expensive three-card shot can be spoiled by one well-timed range change.
builds.why: Tests the upper damage ceiling against a rival who knows the shot is coming and can still react.

builds.name: Trick Shots & Trinkets
builds.plan: Use Basic arrows and flexible Basics to earn Loot, while Hero cards fix their positions or range. Save Arrow Storm for a reliable late-game threat.
builds.sequence: Throw a Rock has effective Range 2–4 through Long Shot. Playing Driving Arrow as a Reaction extends that to 2–6; using Trick Shot instead changes it to 1–4. Neither Reaction earns a Coin; the Rock earns one when it finishes.
builds.weakness: Few high-damage normal Attacks. Keeping every flexible card for later can mean never taking the decisive shot.
builds.why: Tests whether generic economic cards still feel like an archer’s tools because of his passive and Hero reactions.
